_provenance.box: RTX 5070 (sm_120), CUDA 13.3, torch 2.13, N=K=4096, desktop session active
_provenance.method: median of 3 consecutive runs, 30 timed iterations after 10 warmup each
tolerance_rationale: 0.10, derived not guessed. Across the 3 runs the worst observed spread
(max-min)/median was 3.3%, on fused_speedup_vs_bf16.M2048 - a ratio, so it
inherits the bf16 baseline's noise. Absolute timings held to <=0.3%.
10% is ~3x the worst spread: loose enough that a busy desktop does not cry
wolf, tight enough that the +21.7% outlier seen once on gemm_ms.M2048
(0.164 -> 0.1996, immediately after a GreenBoost reinstall and extension
rebuild) is still caught. An earlier draft of this file picked 10% at the
keyboard and called it loose because timings are noisy; the measurement
says they are not, and the number happens to be right for a reason that
why: C-16 decided that build_cutlass_nvfp4_processor stays None on the strength
of these numbers. A decision resting on a measurement should fail loudly
when the measurement moves, and prose in a casebook cannot do that.
Cosine values are deterministic (0.0% spread across runs): a real drop in
cos_vs_dequant is a correctness claim about the CUTLASS scale-factor
